key_highlights: ASX closed the week lower as hawkish US jobs data raised Fed rate-hike odds, pressuring global risk assets and AUD
Australian banks forecast record house price falls; CBA reports home loan applications down 15% since budget, signalling credit contraction
Iron ore sector faces a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical conflict, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX
EV adoption in Australia has passed tipping point (BYD), with EV sales overtaking petrol cars for first time, reshaping energy and auto supply chains
Construction sector under stress: Bathla collapse and ASIC whistleblower review at Big Four accounting firms raise systemic risk flags
Ratings agencies warn on Victoria's soaring debt, adding sovereign credit risk to state-linked infrastructure plays
Small-cap miners (Kaoko, Vanadium Resources, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) showing relative strength

sectors.trend: Iron ore shakeout underway amid geopolitical noise; small-cap gold and critical-mines names (vanadium, rare earths) outperforming majors
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from structural demand shift; Aurum, Kaoko Metals, Vanadium Resources, Power Minerals offer thematic upside in gold and critical minerals

sectors.trend: Credit contraction accelerating: CBA reports 15% drop in home loan applications; banks forecast record house price declines; ASIC whistleblower review at Big Four raises governance concerns
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face NIM compression and rising credit losses; legal loophole allowing CBA/Westpac to overcharge loyal customers invites regulatory risk

sectors.trend: EV sales overtook petrol cars in Australia; BYD confirms tipping point; hidden costs (grid, battery recycling) emerging; Volkswagen cutting 50,000 jobs globally
sectors.implications: WES.AX, AGL.AX, SGP.AX benefit from electrification demand; fuel retailers (WES.AX) face structural decline; battery and charging infrastructure names gain

sectors.trend: Bathla collapse signals broader construction sector fragility; $550m Melbourne freeway upgrade and 'biggest shortcut' negotiations provide offsetting demand
sectors.implications: WBC.AX, CGP.AX, WES.AX (construction arms) face quality-of-earnings risk; government infrastructure spend supports short-term order books

sectors.trend: Ozempic maker in trouble, shifting demand to tablet alternatives; Lululemon cuts forecast on revenue decline; consumer spending under pressure
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, WES.AX, WDW.AX face mixed signals; defensive healthcare (CSL.AX, SGH.AX) remains a portfolio anchor

sectors.trend: AI fears fading (Duolingo, Zeta, Broadcom); Australia faces AI worker shortage; social media algorithm opt-out regulation pending
sectors.implications: ASX-listed tech (W1.AX, XRO.AX) and global AI names benefit; regulatory risk from algorithm opt-out legislation

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce duration exposure; favour cash-flow-positive ASX names; hedge AUD/USD via forward contracts

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Australian housing credit contraction and price decline
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) and construction; monitor CBA/NAB credit loss provisions
Diversify materials exposure toward gold (GOLD.AX, REG.AX) and critical minerals; reduce FMG.AX/BHP.AX weight
Screen construction/infra names for balance-sheet strength; avoid leveraged small-caps
Monitor state-linked infrastructure and utility exposures; favour federal over state bonds

risk_assessment.risk_factor: ASIC whistleblower review at Big Four
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor for regulatory action spillover into listed audit clients

opportunities.rationale: Iron ore shakeout and geopolitical risk drive rotation into gold (Aurum, Kaoko) and critical minerals (Vanadium Resources, Power Minerals, Solstice Minerals)

opportunities.recommendation: Add defensive healthcare and consumer staples
opportunities.rationale: Housing credit contraction and rate uncertainty favour cash-flow defensive names; CSL remains ASX quality anchor

opportunities.recommendation: Position for EV infrastructure and grid upgrade beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: EV sales overtaking petrol cars creates structural demand for charging, battery storage, and grid upgrades

defensive_moves.rationale: Record house price fall forecasts and 15% loan application drop signal prolonged property downturn; Bathla-type failures raise sector contagion risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim iron ore major weightings; hedge AUD/USD
defensive_moves.rationale: Structural iron ore shakeout and hawkish US data pressure AUD and commodity-linked earnings
CBA/Westpac pricing loopholes and ASIC review create regulatory and earnings-overhang risk for financials

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure in the 1–3 month window as global rate-hike fears persist, AUD weakens, and Australian housing credit data deteriorate. Iron ore majors face further downside. Small-cap gold and critical minerals may outperform. RBA on hold but hawkish global backdrop limits domestic easing.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive: 'bull case returns' narrative gains traction if US inflation cools and Fed pivots. EV transition, critical minerals demand, and infrastructure spend ($550m Melbourne freeway, national shortcut) support select sectors. Housing correction may deepen before stabilising. Canada outperforming Australia on per-capita growth is a structural concern.
